core_obligations: Choose the polynomial presentation with kernel J and identify the truncated cotangent complex with the two-term complex (proof lines 2964-2968).
Use finite projectivity of J/J^2 to conclude that the truncation is perfect with tor amplitude in [-1, 0] (proof lines 2969-2973).
Reduce the remaining vanishing to the distinguished triangle for A -> P -> B (proof lines 2974-2980).
Apply the Koszul regularity lemma to L_{B/P} and the polynomial algebra lemma to the left term to finish (proof lines 2980-2983).
difficulty_reason: Counts the author Proposition: for a local complete intersection map A -> B, the cotangent complex L_{B/A} is a perfect complex with tor amplitude in [-1, 0] (source lines 2958-2962). The proof chooses a polynomial presentation P = A[x_1,...,x_n] surjecting onto B with kernel J and uses the identification of the truncated cotangent complex with the two-term complex J/J^2 -> (+)B dx_i; since J/J^2 is finite projective the truncation is perfect with the stated tor amplitude, so it remains to show that the other cohomology groups vanish. That is deduced from the distinguished triangle for A -> P -> B: the left term is computed by the polynomial algebra lemma, and the right term L_{B/P} has cohomology concentrated in degrees -1 and 0 by the Koszul regularity lemma, whence the middle term also vanishes outside those degrees.
